Video editing has nowadays become a conversation.. 

you drop raw footage in a folder, tell Claude Code what you want, and get final.mp4 back. 

its free, open source, 17,000 stars on Github.. it's called video-use. 

and the reason it's different from every "AI video editor" is how it actually works under the hood.. 

it doesn't guess. it transcribes every word you said first, then edits off the actual transcript.

what it does once your footage is in the folder:

- cuts every umm, uh, and false start automatically - kills the dead space between takes - color grades each segment.. warm cinematic, neutral punch, or a custom ffmpeg chain - builds the cut with editor sub-agents, runs the animations in parallel - renders a preview, grades its own work, and iterates until it's clean

and yeah.. it asks before it cuts. 

it shows you the plan in plain english and waits for your yes. 

it's not a black box that spits out a mystery edit.. you stay the director, it does the labor.

▫️ how to start

install the skill in claude code (repo below) 
drop your raw clips in a folder tell it "cut the filler, tighten the pauses, warm cinematic grade" and let it work

And yes,

it's a tool, not a taste replacement. it'll hand you a clean, tight cut, but the creative calls, the hook, the pacing, the story.. that's still you. 

it does the 80% that's grunt work so you spend your time on the 20% that matters.

editing stopped being a skill you grind for years. it's a prompt now.

text:
I don’t ask Claude to “make a video” anymore

I give it 6 small jobs. each one produces one file, and the next job starts from that file

> reference  spec.md
it watches a video I like and writes down why it works: pacing, first motion, cut rhythm

> data  data.json
it pulls the real numbers and keeps the source next to every figure

> story  story.md
one point, one hero number, three beats. before anything moves

> motion  Scene.tsx
it writes every frame as code with Remotion and a motion-design skill

> direct  timing.ts
I give notes in plain words. “title is a beat late”  one line changes

ship  final.mp4
it renders stills, checks them against the spec and the data, then waits for my approval

why small jobs work better:

each step has one clear output, so it’s easy to check
if something looks off, you know exactly which file to fix
nothing gets re-rolled, so the rest of the video stays the same

one big prompt gives you a guess
six small jobs give you a video you can actually edit

full setup, prompt and the 10 open-source skills are in the article

An AI agent built a physics twin of a robot task from a phone video in under an hour. 

This project RoboSimStudio was built on Newton by researchers from UC Berkeley and NVIDIA Robotics. 

Open toolkit, every physics parameter exposed as something a human can slide or an agent can edit.

The demo is a bimanual setup, one arm holding a bar, the other wiping a marker stripe off it with a foam sponge. Input was a smartphone video. 

What's more important no CAD, and no calibrated cameras. Claude and GPT-6 Astra each built a simulation of it independently. One finished in 56 minutes.

Then they ran it on the real robot and the bar support moved. In simulation it had been modelled as fixed, so the sponge kept contact. In reality it shifted and contact was lost.

The agent went back and replaced the fixed constraint with a free rigid body. The revised simulation then reproduced the tipping the original could not.

That is the loop actually closing. The real world found the modelling error and the fix went back into the twin.
